core.description: Practical CTF sandbox profile for triage, scripting, crypto math and constraints, pwn payload generation, reverse triage, forensics, web requests, DNS, image and audio decoding, steganography, OCR, and malware static analysis.

reverse: Static baseline: file, rabin2, readelf, strings, nm, objdump, checksec, inspect_artifact.
Use r2/rabin2 for disassembly, cross-references, function metadata, and binary format questions; use jadx only for APK, DEX, or Java bytecode evidence.
Dynamic cross-check: gdb/gdb-multiarch for state/control flow, strace/ltrace for observable boundaries, qemu-user for foreign architectures.
pwn: Baseline: checksec plus ELF metadata, then reproduce the input/crash path locally before payload construction.
pwntools/pwn, ROPgadget, ropper, r2, gdb/gdb-multiarch, one_gadget, patchelf, seccomp-tools, qemu-user, and binutils support bounded local exploit development.
Remote interaction remains API-side scoped TCP; the sandbox sidecar has no network access.

heavy.description: Opt-in, build-time-only profile for SageMath, automated RSA attacks, large factoring, fast lattice reduction, deeper reverse engineering, symbolic execution, emulation, Frida workflows, and local ML model attacks.

sandboxContract.network: The Docker sidecar is configured with network_mode: none. Remote services must be reached through scoped HTTP/TCP tools in the API process.
sandboxContract.filesystem: Challenge input is mounted read-only; every run receives a dedicated scratchRoot/runs/<run-id> namespace with isolated cwd, HOME, and TMPDIR.
sandboxContract.execution: Commands are structured as program + args + optional stdin. Shell parsing is not used. Run namespaces prevent normal tool-protocol access to another run's scratch files; deployment-level containers or microVMs are required for mutually untrusted tenant kernel isolation.
